{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports a quantitative measure of agreement (cross-species convergence) between functional connectivity changes in thalamic pain in human patients and model macaques, specifically comparing effect sizes of FC changes between species.",
  "arm": "efficacy",
  "arm_evidence": "The study aims to identify cross-species convergence of FC changes associated with thalamic pain, suggesting a potential for understanding therapeutic strategies.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "neurology-stroke",
    "pain"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on 'thalamic pain', which is a type of central poststroke pain (CPSP).",
  "model_type": "induced",
  "model_evidence": "The study uses a macaque model of thalamic pain created by stereotactic microinjection of collagenase into the thalamus.",
  "species": [
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly mentions using 'model macaques' and compares findings between human patients and these macaques.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses functional connectivity (FC) changes as a primary outcome, which are then correlated with clinical pain scores (VAS, SF-MPQ2), representing both biomarker and potentially hard outcome measures."
}
